text:
maria: Heads up — gpupool-eu2 nodes are flipping to NotReady / NoSchedule, started ~10m ago. Seeing a bunch of device-plugin errors in kubelet logs.
kevin: Logs? any obvious kernel/module errors?
sre-laura: paste from one node kubelet: `E0907 12:01:23.456789] device_plugin.go:193] Failed to get device info: open /var/lib/nvidia/driver.sock: permission denied` and later `kubelet: node-labels removed, node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable`
aj: Device plugin pod (nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset) is CrashLoopBackOff on a few nodes. Container logs show: `failed to load kernel module nvidia_virt: -22` and `nvidia-uvm: module not found`
nathan: dmesg snippet from node-03: `nvidia: probe of 0000:3b:00.0 failed with error -22` — looks like kernel/driver ABI mismatch after the image roll 03:50
ops-bot: [deploy-bot] rolling-node-image-update started for gpupool-eu2 (ami: redwood-gpu-2026-08-29-v3)
maria: That AMI is the one we rolled last night. If kernel changed, DKMS/driver kernel headers could be out of sync.
kevin: Confirmed kernel version on affected nodes: `6.6.12-rt` vs driver built for `6.5.x` in the AMI. Oops.
aj: Autoscaler note: nodes are tainted `nvidia.com/gpu-present:NoSchedule` when device plugin fails, so pods are piling up and CA is refusing new nodes because of scale-down/scale-up cooldowns. autoscaler-bot: [cluster-autoscaler] scale-up triggered but failed: insufficient capacity (taints blocking scheduling).
sre-laura: Immediate mitigation: cordon + drain one failing node and replace with a fresh instance using previous AMI. That should get us back to capacity quickly.
maria: I'll cordon/evict a test node now. Command: `kubectl cordon node-03 && kubectl drain node-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
kevin: FYI don't drain if it's running high-priority training jobs — pick a low-util one. Also we should not restart the device-plugin pods until kernel/driver fix applied.
nathan: Created a hotspot runbook entry: `/runbooks/gpu-driver-rollback` and flagged infra-oncall. Will open ops ticket to rebuild AMI with correct driver/kheaders or roll back to previous AMI.
aj: Quick check: `ls -l /var/lib/nvidia/driver.sock` shows root:root 600, plugin runs as rootless user in the pod and expects socket group to be `docker` in older AMI. Permission change could also explain `permission denied` earlier.
maria: Good catch. So two issues: kernel mismatch causing probe fail + socket perms mismatch causing device-plugin to not talk to host driver.
kevin: Which is higher priority? Kernel mismatch will prevent GPUs from being usable even if perms fixed. Prioritize AMI rollback, but permission change could be hot patchable by fixing socket group and restarting plugin.
sre-laura: Action items: 1) maria to patch socket perms + restart daemonset on a test node (hotfix) 2) nathan to start AMI rollback and coordinate with image-builder 3) aj to adjust autoscaler cooldowns to allow immediate scale-up once nodes healthy 4) kevin to run canary nodes with old AMI and new kernel-drivers matched.
maria: On it — patching socket group to `root:nvidia` and restarting plugin: `kubectl -n kube-system delete pod -l name=nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset`
ops-bot: [incident] incident-2026-09-07-gpu-node-degradation created, severity: medium, assigned: infra (maria, nathan)
autoscaler-bot: [cluster-autoscaler] manual override applied by aj: set scale-down-delay to 15m for gpupool-eu2
kevin: Cost note — training jobs are queued in us-east while eu2 is down, might spike inter-region egress and cost if we re-route. Keep finance in loop if projected >$2k/day overage.
nathan: Image-builder started rollback to `redwood-gpu-2026-08-22-v2`. ETA ~40m. Will post when ready.
sre-laura: After rollback we should run `modprobe nvidia && kubectl apply -f nvidia-device-plugin.yaml` on canary node to ensure registration succeeds.
maria: Hotfix on test node fixed permission issue, device-plugin re-registered, node became Ready. Kernel mismatch still present on other nodes.
kevin: Great. Once rollback is done, schedule rolling restart of gpupool with max-unavailable=1 to avoid capacity cliffs.
aj: I'll update the autoscaler policy to reduce throttle and allow faster recovery after kevin's restart plan.
ops-bot: [deploy-bot] image-rollback job started for gpupool-eu2 -> redwood-gpu-2026-08-22-v2
maria: marking node-03 as uncordoned after tests. `kubectl uncordon node-03` :+1:
kevin: Thanks all. Postmortem note: avoid kernel upgrades in AMI without validated driver rebuild; add automated smoke test that probes `nvidia-smi` during image promotion.
sre-laura: I'll own the postmortem and add the smoke test to image pipeline. Closing thread once rollback completes and autoscaler is stable.
kevin: ping when gpupool back to normal capacity.
ops-bot: [incident] incident-2026-09-07-gpu-node-degradation updated: rollback complete, monitoring for 30m
